name: SparkFun Electronics
old_description: Since 2003, SparkFun has been helping turn ideas into reality – whether you’re creating a smart weather station, exploring the frontier of machine learning, building a robot for school or prototyping your first (or tenth) product. No matter your vision or skill level, our open source components, resources and online tutorials are designed to broaden access to innovative technology and make the road to a finished project shorter.
about:
Founded in 2003 in Niwot, Colorado, SparkFun Electronics began as an open-source hardware company aimed at making electronics accessible to engineers, hobbyists, and educators. The company operates from its headquarters in the Boulder area, where it designs and manufactures a wide range of development boards, sensors, and kits under its own brand.

SparkFun develops and sells open-source electronic components, including microcontroller boards, environmental sensors, RFID modules, and wireless communication devices. It also operates a custom kit service that assembles tailored component packages for workshops, classrooms, and virtual learning programs. A subsidiary, SparkPNT, focuses on high-precision positioning, navigation, and timing products built to be durable, future-proof, and repairable. The company employs approximately 140 people and maintains an extensive catalog of both proprietary and third‑party components.

Customers span education, professional engineering, hobbyist, and product‑development sectors. SparkFun supplies components for AI robotics projects using NVIDIA Jetson modules, high‑precision GPS designs with u‑blox receivers, DIY biometric monitors, and community hackathons. Its distributor and reseller program extends volume pricing to partners, while the Qwiic solderless ecosystem enables rapid prototyping across processor and function boards.

The company emphasizes open‑source design, comprehensive documentation, and tutorials to lower barriers to emerging technology. Its stated mission is to provide hardware, services, and resources that make new technology easy to use, with products designed for durability and repairability.
